AutomationNotes: Naming/simple analyzer rules (nullable usage, async-void, unused usings, one-public-type-per-file) are automatable and cheap enough for MSBuild and pre-checkin. Deeper architecture/SOLID rules (layering, dependency direction) cannot be fully automated - static analysis can only heuristically approximate "does one thing" via method-count/complexity thresholds, which produce false positives/negatives. Flag as Add-ManualItem for PR review rather than hard-fail.
Same reasoning as WebAppWebApi. Applies to any C# code in the database solution (e.g. pre/post-deployment scripts written in C#
column8: SQLCLR projects); does not apply to .sql files themselves.

AutomationNotes: Same reasoning as WebAppWebApi, with added emphasis on public-API-surface stability since SOLID violations at the public surface are harder to correct later without a breaking version bump - still a judgment call requiring Add-ManualItem, not something static analysis resolves alone.

Test existence and pass/fail is fully automatable via test-runner exit code; too slow for MSBuild. Whether a change has a "paired" test is only a heuristic (source file changed with no test file touched) and can be wrong in either direction (e.g. comment-only change needs no test; a test elsewhere already covers it) - flag for manual confirmation, don't hard-fail.

Same automation split as WebAppWebApi. Test existence/pass is checked via the database project's test runner (e.g. tSQLt); the "paired test" heuristic is equally unreliable for schema/migration changes and should be Add-ManualItem, not hard-fail.

Same automation split as WebAppWebApi. For a published package, the "paired test" heuristic is weaker still since public-API changes may require new tests in a consumer-facing test suite the diff itself doesn't show - keep as Add-ManualItem.

Secret-pattern scanning, missing [Authorize] attributes, and inline-SQL detection are automatable and belong in pre-checkin/pipeline. Cancellation-token-parameter presence is automatable and cheap enough for MSBuild. Whether AuthN/AuthZ is correctly scoped to an endpoint's real sensitivity is a business-context judgment call static analysis cannot verify - Add-ManualItem, not a hard gate.

Same split as WebAppWebApi for the AuthN/AuthZ- and cancellation-token-bearing C# code in the solution (e.g. maintenance jobs). Inline-SQL and sensitive-data rules apply directly to .sql files as well as C#, both automatable via pattern scanning; whether a given data element is "sensitive" enough to require masking is still a judgment call - Add-ManualItem.

AuthN/AuthZ sections rarely apply directly (a library does not usually own endpoints) but inline-SQL, sensitive-data, and cancellation-token rules still apply to any C# code the library contains. Same automation split as WebAppWebApi - judgment-based classification stays Add-ManualItem.

Existence and pass/fail of a documented perf/load test is automatable but too slow for pre-checkin or MSBuild - pipeline only, likely a separate non-blocking or scheduled stage. Deciding which endpoints require a perf test at all is a judgment call based on expected traffic/criticality and is not automatable - recorded once per endpoint as a manual design decision, not re-derived by tooling.

Same automation split as WebAppWebApi. Deciding which stored procedures/queries require a perf/load test is a judgment call based on expected data volume and query criticality - manual design decision, not automatable.

Same automation split as WebAppWebApi, narrowed further since this file is only Conditional for ClassLibrary - only applies to operations exposed on the package's public API surface. Deciding which public members qualify as "hot-path" is a manual design decision, not automatable.

Presence of structured logging calls at required entry points (controller actions) and existence of a health-check endpoint are both automatable via static analysis of parsed code. Too slow/unnecessary for MSBuild; fits pre-checkin and pipeline.
Same automation and tier reasoning as WebAppWebApi, applied to the long-running maintenance job's entry point and logging calls rather than a controller action.

Presence of the Redis distributed-cache client usage pattern (registration, cache-key construction) is automatable via static analysis. Whether the chosen cache expiration policy is correct for the data's actual volatility is a business-context judgment call static analysis cannot verify - Add-ManualItem, not a hard gate.

Naming conventions for schema objects, presence of required folders (Deployment/, MigrationScripts/, etc. per GlobalSolutionStructureStandards Section 6), and use of parameterized queries over inline SQL are automatable via static analysis of .sql files. Whether a migration script is safe to run against production data (data-loss risk, backward compatibility) requires DBA-level judgment and is not automatable - always Add-ManualItem for migration scripts specifically.

Version-range format in consuming .csproj files ([MAJOR.0, MAJOR+1.0) pattern) and semantic-version bump correctness relative to the prior published version are both automatable by parsing project files and comparing against the last published package version.
YAML schema/lint validation and structural conformance (required stages
column9: retry/condition syntax) are fully automatable via static parsing of the pipeline YAML files.

AutomationNotes: Same automation and tier reasoning as WebAppWebApi - the pipeline YAML structure requirements do not differ by app type at the automation level.
Same automation and tier reasoning as WebAppWebApi, plus the publish/version-bump stage structure specific to package repos, still fully static-parsing checkable.

Fully automatable via existing TypeScript compiler strict-mode checks and ESLint rule violations, run against the SPA client project's changed files. Only relevant when the repo's front end is a SPA client per applicability.

Component/hook file casing, folder-depth limits, and feature-first folder layout are all automatable via static file-path and ESLint-rule checks against the SPA client project's changed files. Only relevant when that SPA client is built with React per applicability.

Feature/hotfix branch-naming pattern and the direct-commit-to-dev/main guard are fully automatable from local branch state (no code parsing needed) - already implemented in ValidationEngine.ps1 at pre-checkin, with pipeline as a backstop for commits that bypass the local hook. Not an MSBuild concern - MSBuild has no branch/commit context.
Same automation and tier reasoning as WebAppWebApi - branch-naming and direct-commit rules do not differ by app type.
Same automation and tier reasoning as WebAppWebApi - branch-naming and direct-commit rules do not differ by app type.

Folder existence, extraneous-folder detection, and folder-naming checks are purely structural filesystem checks against the WebAppWebApi folder set (Section 3-5) - fully automatable and fast enough for all three tiers. MSBuild (Tier0Check.ps1) already implements a naming-convention subset.

Same automation and tier reasoning as WebAppWebApi, checked against the database-project folder set (Section 6: Deployment/, MigrationScripts/, Proposals/, Reports/, Runbooks/, Security/, Tests/) instead of the application folder set. Some folders in that set are optional per the standard's own wording ("may or may not exist"), so absence alone is not a violation - only presence of a folder outside the defined set, or a non-conforming name, is.
Same automation and tier reasoning as WebAppWebApi, checked against the shared-library folder set (Section 7) including the NuGet packaging/versioning-adjacent project layout.
